methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates patient TMA/serum cohorts, TCGA/GSE bioinformatics, co-culture and knockdown/knockout cell systems, DRG neuron cocultures, orthotopic/subcutaneous/liver metastasis models, Rag1-/- mice to isolate ILC3 effects, vagotomy, and combination drug studies with darifenacin/GPR34i/XBP1si plus anti-PD-L1. Mechanistic coherence is built across ACh->ABHD16A->LysoPS->GPR34->AKT->STAT3->IL22->IRE1a->XBP1s->PD-L1 with ChIP and luciferase reporter confirmation. Limitations: many experiments use n=3-5 per group, with no explicit sample size justification, no blinding, and most rescue experiments are single-donor or single-cell-line. Statistical analysis uses t-tests and ANOVA without multiplicity correction despite hundreds of comparisons, and ROC AUC is reported without 95% CIs.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study combining mouse models with translational biomarker assessments in patient serum/tissues (LoE 5). Clinical relevance is moderate: it identifies serum LysoPS (AUC 0.92) and IL22 (AUC 0.85) as potential diagnostic biomarkers and proposes darifenacin (FDA-approved muscarinic antagonist) combined with anti-PD-L1 as a repurposing strategy for gastric cancer. However, translation requires validation in larger patient cohorts and formal phase trials; the findings are not directly practice-changing at present.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies due to the extensive animal work. Reporting is thorough for cell lines (RRIDs, authentication), antibodies (detailed panel with RRIDs), ethics approvals (IACUC and human Ethics Committee numbers), and methods for key assays. ARRIVE gaps: no sample-size justification, no blinded outcome assessment, no randomization statement for treatment groups, and unclear primary endpoint pre-specification. Data availability statement is not shown; GSE163558 is referenced for external scRNA-seq but no deposition of the study's own RNA-seq data, metabolomics, or cytokine arrays is mentioned. Human subject consent and IRB numbers are provided.

novelty_literature.justification: The work links vagus nerve signaling, lipase ABHD16A/LysoPS, and ILC3 biology with UPR-mediated PD-L1 upregulation in gastric cancer, an integrated neuro-metabolic-immune axis that has not been previously described in this tumor type. It builds on the authors' prior ABHD16A metastasis paper (Yang 2021) and prior LysoPS-ILC3 work (Wang 2021 on tissue repair) but extends to a procarcinogenic TME context with mechanistic and therapeutic rescue experiments. The diagnostic biomarker proposal adds translational novelty. Not first-in-class paradigm shift, but a substantive mechanistic extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is densely written but well-structured, with a clear linear mechanistic narrative from clinical observation through signaling dissection to therapeutic rescue. Figures systematically progress through each node in the proposed axis. Some long paragraphs and occasional minor grammatical issues (e.g., 'IL22 irritates UPR') and one reference to 'nicotinamide' in the tissue specimens section appears misplaced. Overall the scientific logic is easy to follow.

key_strengths: Integrative neuro-metabolic-immune mechanistic chain (ACh->ABHD16A->LysoPS->GPR34->AKT->STAT3->IL22->IRE1a->XBP1s->PD-L1) with in vivo rescue at each node
Use of Rag1-/- mice to isolate ILC3-specific IL22 contribution and CD90.2 depletion strategies
Repurposing-ready combination strategy with FDA-approved darifenacin plus anti-PD-L1
Clinical biomarker data in patient serum (LysoPS AUC 0.92, IL22 AUC 0.85) linked to PNI
ChIP and luciferase reporter evidence for direct XBP1s-CD274 transcriptional regulation
key_concerns: Statistical framework lacks multiplicity correction, effect sizes/CIs, and ROC confidence intervals despite extensive multiple testing
ARRIVE checklist gaps: no explicit sample-size justification, randomization, or blinding statements
Small cohort sizes (n=3-5) for many in vivo rescue experiments limit generalizability
Data availability for RNA-seq, metabolomics, and cytokine arrays not addressed
Reference to 'no patients received nicotinamide' in tissue specimens section appears to be a typo/error warranting attention
Diagnostic biomarker performance requires independent validation cohort before clinical claims
chief_reviewer.rationale: A mechanistically rich, clinically grounded gastric cancer immunology study warrants Tier 2 acceptance (Cancer Research, Clinical Cancer Research, Nature Communications-oncology). It is not paradigm-shifting given existing ACh-tumor and LysoPS-GPR34 literature, and statistical/reporting rigor needs minor revisions; the breadth of in vivo rescue and translational biomarker data is strong.
